caption: Everyone assumes R78 000 means sorted. I still hit zero before payday. What does yours actually leave you?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R78 000
p/m salary
Living in Cape Town
slides.body:
Male, 32
Living with my partner, no kids
Job: Software engineer
Net salary: R78 000 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 2 bed in Sea Point, parking bay, levies
slides.body: Cape Town rent is its own tax. I pay more for this flat than my brother pays on his bond in Bloem.

slides.title: Eating out & delivery
slides.includes: Lunches, weekends, and the delivery apps
slides.body: I guessed R3 000. It was R7 100. Nine hundred rand of that was delivery fees alone.

slides.title: Retirement annuity & TFSA
slides.body: This is the number I lead with when someone asks if I am responsible with money.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: I bought it the month I got promoted. That is the whole reasoning, written down honestly.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Woolworths mostly, Checkers when I plan ahead
slides.body: I do not plan ahead often. The convenience shop on the corner knows me by name.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Family support, credit card & personal loan, medical aid & gym, petrol & tolls, electricity & levies, phone & subscriptions, funeral policy
slides.body: R24 300 on things I have never once looked at as a group. That is nearly a third of my salary.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R78 000. On paper that is a good month. In practice the account is at zero by the 27th and I cannot tell you where it went.

slides.title: A bigger salary did not make it clearer
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

The delivery fees on their own came to R900 a month.

No bank login needed.
